headline: Bitcoin is holding near $60,000 on Sunday evening after Saturday's crash to a two-year low, with fear still extreme and US stocks reopening Monday ahead of a short holiday week full of data.

market.asOf: Prices from CoinMarketCap coin pages, read by this desk at about 15:56 UTC on Sun 22 Nov (22:56 Bangkok). CoinMarketCap's pages showed slightly different figures in different places, so treat the 24h changes as rough. Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 12 out of 100, "Extreme Fear", on the Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index (read at about 15:56 UTC), the same as the day before and 13 a week ago. CoinMarketCap's own Fear and Greed Index read 8 out of 100.

stories.title: Bitcoin steadies near $60,000 after crashing to a two-year low
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell to its lowest price since September 2024 on Saturday, then bounced more than 9% back above $60,000. On Sunday it has stayed close to $60,000, helped by traders who had bet on falling prices being forced to buy back. It is still about 12% lower than a week ago.
points: Bitcoin fell as low as $55,130, its lowest since September 2024, then rose more than 9% to about $60,300, per CoinDesk.
Bitcoin was about $60,424 on Sunday morning, down 12.53% on the week, with the whole crypto market worth about $2.03 trillion, per crypto.news.

Forced selling of leveraged bets totalled about $1.8 billion over 24 hours, $1.3 billion of it from bets on higher prices, per CoinDesk citing CoinGlass; crypto.news cites the Kobeissi Letter at about $2.7 billion.
Then the squeeze reversed: more than $400 million of bets on lower prices were force-closed over 28 hours, per KuCoin News citing WhaleInsider.
CoinDesk says traders see Monday's US stock open as the next test of the bounce.

stories.title: US bitcoin funds lose about $1.25 billion for a third straight $1 billion week; Saylor hints at another buy
stories.summary: Money kept leaving US spot bitcoin ETFs, the funds that let people buy bitcoin through a normal brokerage account. It is the third week in a row of outflows above $1 billion. Strategy, which holds 850,849 bitcoin bought at an average of $75,452 each, saw its chairman hint on Sunday at another purchase.
points: Bitcoin ETFs lost $1.25 billion over 16-20 Nov and ether ETFs $221.7 million, per crypto.news using Farside data; Incrypted, using SoSoValue, put the bitcoin figure at $1.24 billion.
Incrypted says it is the third straight week above $1 billion, with more than $3.59 billion out over the three weeks.
On Thursday 19 Nov BlackRock's IBIT lost $541.1 million, its biggest daily outflow since launch, per CEO Economy.
Michael Saylor posted "The dots aren't done" on Sunday, his usual hint before a purchase; nothing is confirmed until Strategy files, per crypto.news.
Strategy held 850,849 BTC at an average cost of $75,452 as of 15 Nov, per crypto.news.

stories.title: Inflation data, a likely Fed hike and a big options expiry crowd a short holiday week
stories.summary: Traders widely expect the Fed to raise rates again in December, so Wednesday's US inflation data matters more than usual. US markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving, and a large batch of bitcoin options expires Friday.
points: October PCE inflation and Q3 GDP are both due Wed 25 Nov; core PCE is expected at 3.2% a year against 3.1% before, per Newsquawk.
Rate-hike odds: 24/7 Wall St put the chance of a quarter-point December hike at about 92% on 21 Nov; BigGo, citing futures markets, put it at 96.9% on 20 Nov.
Bitcoin options covering 112,323 BTC, about $6.76 billion, expire on Deribit on Fri 27 Nov at 08:00 UTC, per Cryptoticker (Deribit data from 21 Nov).
On Friday the Nasdaq fell 5.28% and the S&P 500 3.70%, and the 2-year Treasury yield is about 4.7%, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: TRUMP memecoin dinner draws far less interest
briefs.summary: Only 130 wallets holding a combined $8.6 million qualified for Sunday's dinner, against about $148 million for the first one, and one holder qualified with a $518 buy, per crypto.news citing Reuters.

briefs.title: Chainflip hack: bounty deadline Monday
briefs.summary: The loss includes 122.86 BTC, 520.22 ETH, 3.25 million USDC and 758,141 USDT, up from a first estimate of $4.86 million; Chainflip offers the attacker 10% if 90% is returned by 18:38 UTC on Mon 23 Nov, per Cointelegraph.

briefs.title: Kalshi faces a Monday court hearing in New York
briefs.summary: A Manhattan state court hears New York Attorney General Letitia James's request for a restraining order on Mon 23 Nov at 11:30am ET; Kalshi says it would shut its exchange nationwide, the AG's office says that is not its aim, per The Block.

briefs.title: iPhone ad attack targeted crypto wallets
briefs.summary: Security firm Confiant traced more than 480 malicious ad domains that could steal wallet recovery phrases on older, unpatched iPhones; no working exploit for iOS 26 was found, so keeping your phone updated is the fix, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Solana drops its "beta" label
briefs.summary: Solana's mainnet moves to version 1.0 with nothing for users to do, and US spot SOL ETFs took in about $4.4 million over 16-20 Nov, ending six weeks of outflows, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Coins.ph stops transfers to self-custody wallets
briefs.summary: The Philippine exchange stopped deposits and withdrawals to wallets users control themselves from 19 Nov, citing Travel Rule compliance, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Strategy leaves MSCI indexes at the end of November
briefs.summary: Strategy is removed from the MSCI USA, World and ACWI indexes at the close of 30 Nov; MSCI-linked funds held about 13 million of its shares, per 24/7 Wall St.

briefs.title: BTCS warns of liquidation risk on its Aave loan
briefs.summary: The Nasdaq-listed company had about $54 million of ether-backed Aave debt as of 19 Nov and warned the collateral could be liquidated if prices fall further, per The Defiant.

calendar.event: US PCE inflation (Oct), Q3 GDP (second estimate), durable goods and jobless claims
calendar.note: Core PCE is expected at 3.2% a year (prior 3.1%), per Newsquawk. Q3 GDP is expected at 3.5% after 3.4% before, per FXEmpire. Weekly jobless claims come out on Wednesday this week; 201K is expected after 203K, per FXEmpire.
The Fed's survey of business conditions around the country, per the Fed. New home sales come out earlier the same day at 10:00am ET (22:00 Bangkok), per FXEmpire.
On Friday 27 Nov US stocks close early at 1:00pm ET (01:00 Sat Bangkok), per LiteFinance. Crypto trades all day, but thin trading can mean bigger swings.

calendar.event: Monthly bitcoin options expiry on Deribit
calendar.note: About $6.76 billion of bitcoin options (112,323 BTC) expire, with the "max pain" level at $73,000, per Cryptoticker using Deribit data from 21 Nov.
The last jobs report before the Fed decision, per the BLS schedule. November CPI is Thu 10 Dec, the day after the Fed decision, per the BLS.

calendar.event: Next Fed meeting and rate decision
calendar.note: Two-day meeting 8-9 Dec; the decision is at 2:00pm ET on Wed 9 Dec (02:00 Thu Bangkok), per the Fed. Fed officials stop public comment on policy from Sat 28 Nov, under the Fed's blackout rule. 24/7 Wall St put the chance of a quarter-point hike at about 92% on 21 Nov.
